title: Control of Administrative Rule-Making — Legislative, Judicial and Procedural

content.overview: Control over administrative rule-making is exercised through parliamentary laying and scrutiny, publication and consultation requirements, administrative hierarchical control, and judicial review for ultra vires and constitutional defects.
content.glance: Identify which control channel is engaged — legislative, procedural, administrative or judicial — and apply the standards specific to that channel.
content.study: Democratic control of subordinate legislation includes laying rules before the legislature and committee scrutiny where the parent Act so provides. Publication ensures notice. Consultation may be statutory or administrative. Courts control rules through judicial review. Effective control is cumulative. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in the parent Act and Constitution. Do not treat BSA 2023 as the source of this doctrine.

sections.heading: Legislative Control
sections.body: Laying requirements, affirmative/negative resolutions and committee scrutiny.

sections.heading: Publication and Consultation
sections.body: Notice to the public and stakeholder input where required.

sections.heading: Administrative Control
sections.body: Internal vetting, hierarchical approval and departmental scrutiny.

sections.heading: Judicial Control
sections.body: Ultra vires, rights review and reasonableness where applicable.

sections.heading: Interaction of Controls
sections.body: No single channel is exclusive; gaps in one may be filled by another.

examples.title: Laid but ultra vires
examples.body: A rule is laid before Parliament but exceeds the parent Act. Laying does not cure ultra vires; judicial review remains available.

examples.title: Publication failure
examples.body: Required publication is omitted. Procedural control and possible invalidity are engaged.

hypotheticals.question: If a rule is laid before Parliament can it still be challenged in court?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Laying does not cure ultra vires or constitutional defects.

hypotheticals.question: Is publication a mere formality?
hypotheticals.analysis: Lack of required publication can affect validity and fairness.

distinctions.title: Legislative control vs judicial control
distinctions.left: Political and procedural scrutiny by the legislature

misconceptions.trap: If a rule is laid before Parliament it cannot be challenged in court.
misconceptions.correction: Laying does not cure ultra vires or constitutional defects.
Lack of required publication can affect validity and fairness.

cases.name: Indian Express Newspapers (Bombay) Pvt. Ltd. v Union of India
cases.facts: Validity of delegated legislation imposing customs duty on newsprint.
cases.issue: Grounds for judicial review of subordinate legislation.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Delegated legislation is open to judicial review on constitutional and statutory grounds.
cases.holding: Judicial-review framework for subordinate legislation articulated.
cases.relevance: Leading authority already in the file on control of delegated legislation.

cases.name: State of Tamil Nadu v P. Krishnamurthy
cases.issue: Grounds permitting courts to invalidate delegated legislation.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Subordinate legislation may be challenged for lack of competence, constitutional violation, failure to conform to enabling statute, repugnancy and manifest arbitrariness.

cases.name: Cellular Operators Association of India v Telecom Regulatory Authority of India
cases.facts: Regulations made by a statutory regulator reviewed.
cases.issue: How judicial review operates against expert regulatory subordinate legislation.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Regulatory expertise does not immunise subordinate legislation from judicial review.
cases.holding: Regulations scrutinised against the governing statute.
cases.relevance: Authority already in the file on modern regulatory rulemaking.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a rulemaking-control problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify control channel. II. Apply channel-specific standards. III. Note interaction of controls. IV. Formulate remedy.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Channel engaged; statutory requirement; judicial-review ground if challenged; precise relief.

examTips: State that laying does not cure ultra vires.
